$comment: THE CLASSIFICATION OF EVERY FIXTURE FAMILY THE MAQUETTE ENGINE DECLARES, and it is TOTAL: a family the extractor finds and this file does not name is a violation, and so is a name here the extractor cannot find. That is what makes the guard reading it impossible to pre-satisfy — it holds a NAMED INVENTORY, never a count. A floor placed at today's number is satisfied by construction on the day it is written and can only ever catch a later decrease, which is the shape B-075 found five times over. Regenerate the inventory with `node scripts/extract-maquette-fixtures.mjs --list`; the CLASS is a judgement and is never generated.

$classes.served: server state — the operator's system holds it. A seed derives from it and a handler serves it
$classes.asset: artwork, poster and trailer maps — served as part of a media payload, never as a resource of its own
$classes.interface: WHAT THE INTERFACE OWNS and a server must never send: labels, tones, orderings, icon paths, page sizes, timings. Routing one of these through a mock would have the interface asking a server for its own words. They stay where they are; L09 moves the copy to i18n and the rest into the components. The class is defined by OWNERSHIP rather than by being words — a long-press delay belongs to the interface exactly as a label does
$classes.unserved: not served, with the reason written out

$converted: A FAMILY THE ENGINE NO LONGER DECLARES, because the surface that read it now reads the mock layer instead (D5 — the engine dies by subtraction, surface by surface). Its class is unchanged: it is still `served`, and its seed is still what the layer answers with. What changes is WHAT HOLDS THE SEED. `--arm correspondence` compared it against the engine's own literal, and that literal is gone — so for a converted family that arm has nothing left to compare and says so by name rather than passing over it in silence, which would be the vacuity this whole file is built against. Two instruments still hold it: `--arm schema` validates it against the contract, and the ORACLE holds the rendering it produces at zero divergence — which is the stronger of the two, since it reads the bytes all the way to the screen. The value of `converted` names the wave and the surface, so the day somebody asks « when did this stop being checkable against the engine » the answer is in the file.
